title: Q-ULTRA-self_shipping-3: Self-originated releases out of bounds: restructure: find why the executor's items fail and change its route (model rung, patch format, item size)
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** essential variable `self_shipping` out of bounds (reading 0.214; limits 1.0 to None)
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation ultrastability --check
**Status:** closed

ULTRASTABILITY-1 second-order step: restructure: find why the executor's items fail and change its route (model rung, patch format, item size). Rowan's biggest goal: the server itself originates and ships substantive changes daily (SELF-REFERENCE-1). Counted from git by foundation/yearsim.py self_commits: executor or own-agent commits on main with at least 10 changed lines of code outside ledgers and generated data. A one-line import removal is upkeep, not a release (NO-TRIVIAL-COMMITS).

size: M

**Closing probe:** `python3 -m foundation ultrastability --tick` reads `self_shipping` inside its bounds.


**Vacuous:** 2026-11-21T23:11:19Z vacuous: the probe was never recorded failing on this item, so its pass cannot show the defect is gone; rewrite the probe so it fails while the defect exists

**Disposition:** fixed (executor-failed, 2026-11-21T23:43:01Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** the executor failed 3 consecutive runs on this item; last reason: RuntimeError: checks failed after 2 attempts: the reply was not valid JSON with a files list: ValueError: need 1..8 files, got 31. Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).

**Evidence:** 2026-11-22T13:51:17Z closing probe passed after the item was disposed: ultrastability ok: two loops, every variable has a bound and a second-order step
